q-38662.name: Question 1
q-38662.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
q-38662.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 7 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((2-\lambda )(-2-\lambda )-5(-1)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{0\pm \sqrt{{0}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 1}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135532.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 9 \\ 5 & 6-\lambda  & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )^{2}-9(-1)) & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +10) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=6.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{(2)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 10}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{-36}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm 6\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-1\pm 3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135538.name: Question 3
q-135538.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1+3\text{i} \\ 4+3\text{i} \\ 2-7\text{i} \\ -1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1-6\text{i} \\ 4+4\text{i} \\ 2+3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2+5\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=2\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135538.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 & -6 \\ 2 & -7 & 4 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[1+3i4+3i2−7i−1−2i],v3=[−11−6i4+4i2+3i],B=[2500−5200000200−20] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=2+5i and λ3=2i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[431−62−74413−10−1−223]
b
[43−612−744130−1−1−232]
c
[431−613−10−1−2232−744]
d
[31−10341−6−7244−2−123]
e
[13−10431−62−744−1−223]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[2500−5200000200−20], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[13−10431−62−744−1−223].

$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2-2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3+5\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 & -3\end{aligned}],

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ -7 & 3 & 2 & -6 \\ 4 & -1 & 4 & -6 \\ -6 & -4 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135667.name: Question 5
q-135667.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ 1+3\text{i} \\ 4-7\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2+7\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135667.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 5 \\ -4 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vectors v1 and v2 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[3−41],v2=[−2+5i1+3i4−7i],B=[5000270−72] The vectors v1 and v2 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=2+7i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[8−25−413−54−7]
b
[3−15−46314−7]
c
[3−25−41314−7]
d
[3−2621374−1]
e
[3−70−13354−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[5000270−72], we deduce that the first column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v1 and the second and third columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v2:

P=[3−25−41314−7]
